selection: Three first cases target articles previously supported by hypothetical scenarios and component-level photos. Each adds a problem, a project-specific decision, a reported outcome and a transferable lesson.

sources.title: Coffield, Lappano and Mella: Brock Environmental Center, High Performing Buildings (2016)
sources.scope: Project design-team account: coastal conditions, mixed cross/stack ventilation, window operation and predicted natural-ventilation hours. The prediction is not treated as a measurement.

sources.title: WBDG: Brock Environmental Center project-team case study
sources.scope: Project-team submission: airflow and controls strategy, monitoring and reported occupant-satisfaction findings; not an independent cross-flow-only performance test.

sources.title: Passivhaus Trust: How to Build a Passivhaus, second edition (2023), Reform Cottage, printed p. 53
sources.scope: Reform Cottage construction case: connected wall/roof insulation, window positioning, 2018 EnerPHit certification and reported 0.31 ACH at 50 Pa airtightness.

sources.title: 21 Degrees: Reform Cottage EnerPHit, Herefordshire (2021)
sources.scope: Participating supplier and ventilation designer account: project team, existing construction, junction work and reported airtightness. Heating-need data are not presented as metered savings.

sources.title: cepezed: Dismantling a building and rebuilding it elsewhere (18 September 2025)
sources.scope: Architect account of completed courthouse reassembly as an office and knowledge lab; layout and solar-control glazing changes.

sources.title: Rijksvastgoedbedrijf: Circulariteit loont, hoe een tijdelijk gebouw twee levens kreeg (13 April 2026)
sources.scope: Original public client account: contract, residual-value incentives, detachable components, storage and second use in Enschede.

cases.heading: Brock Environmental Center — a documented mixed-mode building

evidence.claim: Low and high openings on north and south faces; weather-linked window operation; cross flow combined with stack ventilation.
Over 11% of occupied annual hours predicted for natural-ventilation cooling.
Project-team account reports environmental measurements and occupant satisfaction above comparison benchmarks.

evidence.claim: External wall insulation connected to roof insulation; windows placed within the insulation zone and sealed with tapes and membranes.

evidence.unit: air changes per hour at 50 Pa
evidence.claim: Reported achieved airtightness; guide records EnerPHit certification in 2018.
Owner-led retrofit of an extended nineteenth-century stone cottage, including ventilation design.

cases.heading: Amsterdam’s temporary courthouse — a completed second use
cases.project: Temporary Amsterdam Courthouse, reassembled at Kennispark Twente
cases.design_credit: cepezed and project partners; disassembly and reassembly by Lagemaat and Groothuis Bouwgroep

evidence.claim: Contract included design, construction, dismantling and reuse; residual component value formed part of the financial arrangement.
Architect’s September 2025 account reports reassembly in Enschede as an office and knowledge lab, with a changed layout and relocated solar-control glazing.
Client and contractor describe dismantling beginning in 2021; architect describes dismantling in 2022. Article uses 2021–22 for the process.

image_limits: No reviewed reusable project photo was found for Reform Cottage; the primary technical guide links directly to its construction photographs.
No reviewed reusable photograph of the temporary courthouse was found; the architect’s reassembly account links to actual project photographs. Existing component photos retain their own headings.
excluded_claims: Brock’s predicted natural-ventilation hours are not labelled as measured savings or cross-flow-only performance.
Reform Cottage’s published heating-need figure is not labelled as metered consumption.
The courthouse’s reported percentage reuse has no mass or cost basis stated in the consulted account, so the article emphasizes completed reassembly instead.
No numerical carbon saving is asserted for the courthouse.
